title: Lights Out Tonight
intro: A text from your electricity company. It looks urgent.
Tap anything that looks odd to sniff it closer. Pin what is suspicious, clear what is harmless.
When you are sure, decide what to do.

notify.text: Your power will be cut tonight at 9:30 PM…

screen.context: You paid your last bill on the 3rd.

msg.text: Your power will be cut tonight at 9:30 PM.

msg: He will send you an app to

unpaid.label: Says the bill is unpaid
unpaid.lens: You paid your last bill on the 3rd.
unpaid.why: A claim that does not match your own records is a warning sign. Check your bill.

cut.label: Cut-off tonight
cut.why: Real utilities do not demand same-day payment to avoid disconnection.

number.label: A new number to call
number.lens: The number is not the one on your bill.
number.why: Use the number on your bill or the company's website, never one from a text.

app.label: Installs an app
app.lens: The "officer" will send you an app to update your details.
app.why: No real company needs you to install an app from a message. It can give a stranger control of your phone.

sender.label: Company name
sender.why: A name is easy to copy. It proves nothing alone.

actions.label: Call the number now to save my power
Check my last bill and call the number printed on it
Report it as a scam and delete it

trap.title: Call 70000 55123
trap.ask: The "officer" says: "Install this app and share the code it shows, then I will clear your bill." The app shows your screen to the caller.

block_report.line: Reported and deleted. Your real power stayed on, and the number was flagged for others.

verify.line: The number on your bill reached the real company. They said: "Your account is paid, and we never cut power by text." Case cracked.

ignore.line: You stayed safe. The lights stayed on, but the same text is landing on thousands of other phones.

go_ahead.line: The app let the caller see your phone. They read your bank codes and emptied your account.

what_if.go_ahead: Checking the number printed on your own bill takes a minute, and it would have reached the real company.
what_if.ignore: Reporting takes two taps and helps others avoid the same call.
what_if.verify: Checking was smart. Reporting the text as well protects other people.

golden_rule: A same-day cut-off threat is a pressure trick. Use the number on your bill, never a number from a text.

quick_check.q: A text says your power will be cut tonight unless you call a number and install an app. What do you do?

options.text: Call quickly, it is only tonight
Install the app but do not share a code
Check your bill and use the number printed on it, and report the text
Pay in gift cards to be safe

quick_check.explain: Real utilities do not demand same-day payment. Your own bill has the right number.

hints.nudge: Does the text match what you know about your last bill?

rows.v: Not the one on your bill

rows.k: Real utilities demand same-day payment to avoid disconnection?

rows.v: Use the number on your bill or the company's website
